newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan minister cancels Korea trip over Peru crisis.
newsitem.headline: Japan minister cancels Korea trip over Peru crisis.

text.p: Japanese Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda said on Tuesday he had cancelled a planned visit to South Korea this week due to the hostage crisis in Lima.
"After consulting Prime Minister (Ryutaro) Hashimoto and the South Korean government, I decided to cancel my visit scheduled for December 26 and 27," Ikeda told a news conference.

Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) guerrillas stormed the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima last Tuesday during a reception to mark Emperor Akihito's birthday, taking more than 500 hostages.
After freeing a large number of captives, the rebels were still holding at gunpoint dozens of top Peruvian government officials and about 30 high-ranking Japanese businessmen and diplomats.

The foreign minister had planned to hold talks with his South Korean counterpart Yoo Chong-ha ahead of a summit meeting in Japan in late January between Hashimoto and South Korean President Kim Young-sam.
Ikeda, who spent four days in Lima as Japan's on-the-spot adviser, returned to Tokyo on Monday evening.

Ikdeda said he did not even rule out the possibility that the hostage crisis could force the cancellation of the summit meeting in the resort city of Beppu on Japan's southern island of Kyushu on January 25 and 26.
"It all hinges on the developments in the incident in Peru," Ikeda said.
